n6281417974: Weldon Spring is named for John Weldon, a frontiersman who settled beside a spring here on a Spanish land grant back in the seventeen-nineties, when this was still Spanish territory. The town itself was laid out in the eighteen-hundreds. Then came the big twist. In World War Two the Army moved out three little towns, Howell, Hamburg and Toonerville, and built what was called the largest explosives factory in the United States, making TNT. In nineteen fifty-five the Atomic Energy Commission added a uranium processing plant. The cleanup made national news and took years; in two thousand one all the waste was sealed inside a giant rock-covered hill, seventy-five feet tall and forty-one acres wide. Today that's the famous attraction: you can climb the stairs to the top for the view, and visit the interpretive center that opened in a new building in twenty twenty-two. Around it, the old factory land is now the Busch and Weldon Spring conservation areas, with lakes, deer and the Katy Trail along the Missouri River.
